fields.System.Title: INV-5 — Reservations
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Promise specific stock to a specific order line, so that two orders can never be promised the
same unit.

Scope

In. Creating, releasing, and consuming reservations. Reporting orphans.

Out. Deciding which stock to reserve — that is [OUT-2](../OUT/OUT-2-allocation.md).

Design notes

Reservations leak, and this is the feature where you decide whether they will.

A reservation is created in one place and released in many: on ship, on cancel, on short pick,
on quality hold, on order amendment, on wave cancellation, on transfer cancellation. Miss one
path and reserved stock accumulates silently. Availability decays over months with no visible
cause, and eventually someone finds a product with 500 on hand and 12 available.

Build INV-502 alongside INV-501, never after. And build INV-504 in the same stage,
because the report is the only thing that will detect the path you missed.

Consume means both fields together. A pick reduces on-hand and reserved in one statement. A
path that reduces one without the other produces negative availability, which downstream code
handles unpredictably.

The invariant to assert everywhere: the sum of reservation rows equals qty_reserved on the
balance, and 0 <= qty_reserved <= qty_on_hand.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Reservation not released on cancel | [doc 09 §5.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Reservation not consumed on pick | [doc 09 §5.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Partial pick leaves a hanging remainder | [doc 09 §5.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| On-hand and reserved diverge | [doc 09 §2.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Reservations surviving their order | [doc 09 §5.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
